walkthroughs.body_html:
Comparative Study (HL Extension) — a core area of Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Comparative Study (HL Extension) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Comparative Study (HL Extension).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who developed iconological method in Studies in Iconology 1939?
options: Heinrich Wolfflin
Erwin Panofsky
Alois Riegl
Aby Warburg

mcqs.q: Whose 1998 Art and Agency treats artworks as social agents?
options: Bourdieu
Gell
Baxandall
Belting

mcqs.q: What is the central innovation of Cubism?
options: Using only blue and green.
Showing an object from multiple viewpoints simultaneously on a flat surface.
Painting everything as cubes.
Painting on canvas.

mcqs.q: What did Renaissance artists rediscover that medieval art lacked?
options: Linear perspective and naturalistic representation of the human body.
The use of colour.
Painting on canvas.
He painted indoor scenes.

mcqs.q: What did Pollock mean by his drip paintings being 'in the painting'?
options: Painting on canvas.
He painted indoor scenes.
He worked from all sides, making the act of painting central to the meaning.
He literally fell into wet paint.
